utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom, after quite a while of absence and recess. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We had a delayed start due to technical problems. Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm informed that the indication in the courtroom of whether we are in closed or in open session is not properly functioning and that we were in open session for all of the time, despite the little monitor telling us that we were supposed to be in closed session. Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours. We are ready to call the next witness. I wanted to advise the Chamber that I had estimated one and a half hours to examine this witness. Having reviewed the materials quite carefully, it appears to me quite clear that I will not be able to examine him in that period of time so we would be asking to revise the estimate. I'll do my best to cut and trim as I go, and I will hopefully be able to advise the Chamber more precisely how long I will be able to -- I will be examining him by the end of the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, let's then wait and see what the new estimate will be. May I take it that your witness is Mr. Dusan Janc?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time for the following. On the 26th of July, Defence has filed a request for an additional 30 days to file its response to the Prosecution's motion to admit evidence from the bar table concerning the Foca municipality. The Chamber granted this request informally on the 30th of July and now takes the opportunity to put on the record that the new deadline for the response is the 26th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you. May I invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Please be seated. You are already. You'll first be examined by Mr. Vanderpuye. You'll find him to your right. Mr. Vanderpuye is, as most likely you'll be aware of, is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning again. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And good morning to you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just so that we can get started correctly, could you state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: My name is Dusan Janc.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just so that you can provide a little bit of background for the Chamber, could you tell us what your current employment is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Currently I'm with the Office of Internal Oversight Services, this is a United Nations office, and I'm based in Nairobi. I'm an investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How long have you been in that particular assignment?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I've been in Nairobi since 1st of August, 2011.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to acquaint the Chamber with a bit of your professional background. Can you tell us how you began your career?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I joined the police force of the Republic of Slovenia in 1993 as a police officer. After a year I was promoted to a criminal investigator at the police station. Then in 2000 I was promoted to a criminal investigator at the regional level where I -- when I deal -- dealt with organised crime. Between June 2003 and 2004, I was -- I spent a year in European Union Police Mission in Bosnia-Herzegovina as an advisor to criminal investigation department of the Republic of Srpska, and then I returned back to my national police forces in Slovenia. And on 1st of June, 2006, I joined the ICTY Office of the Prosecutor as an investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In your experience in your national jurisdiction, what kinds of investigations did you conduct or participate in, what kind of crimes other than, I assume, organised crimes?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I did investigate all sorts of crimes from minor criminal offences like thefts, fraud, and this kind of crimes when I was at the police station level, and then when I joined the criminal organised crime department I was in charge of more serious crimes including smuggling and acts of terrorism and also a part of homicide department crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in your assignment as an advisor in the RS, Republika Srpska, what specifically did you do?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: European Union Police Mission, EUPM, was a mentoring and monitoring mission in Bosnia-Herzegovina so it was advisory role to the criminal investigation department of the Republika Srpska, in terms of how to perform the professional duties in a properly manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was that in relation to all types of criminal investigations or certain -- certain specific ongoing investigations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It was related to all crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When you joined the Office of the Prosecutor at the ICTY in 2011 as an investigator, what was your assignment?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: As soon as I joined the Office of the Prosecutor, I was attached to the team of Srebrenica investigation and I've been involved with this investigation throughout my career here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that would have been five years from 2006 to 2011, is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Correct, five years and two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Were you involved in the investigation of what specific cases? Rather, let me rephrase that. What specific cases were you involved in the investigation concerned?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: So they -- as I told it was investigation related to the events which occurred after the fall of Srebrenica. But if you're asking me about the cases, the trial cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Which cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yeah. This was -- first when I joined it was Popovic case, Popovic et al case. Then I was involved with the Tolimir case, and I did testify also in Karadzic case last year, and now I'm testifying in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And during the course of your involvement in these -- in the Srebrenica investigation for the five years that you were with the Office of the Prosecutor, what types of materials did you review, did you investigate, research, that kind of thing?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: You mean in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In general.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It was all sorts of material which was collected over the years, also which was collected during the time I spent with the Office of the Prosecutor. So which basically mean documentation obtained during the year, evidence on different sorts of criminal activities, then witness statements, documents provided to the OTP through different requests for assistance, all -- various types of internal documents like documents produced by different investigators on investigations itself, which means basic reports, analyses on findings, so these are the type of evidence I've been reviewing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you undertake any missions to the field and, in particular, in respect of the grave sites that are alleged to be part or related to the crimes charged in the Srebrenica events?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. I did visit grave sites back in -- if I'm not mistaken, in October or November 2007. At that time, I visited with my colleagues all the grave sites known at the time, either being already exhumed or not, and were related to Srebrenica events.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now you mentioned that you testified in the Popovic, Tolimir and Karadzic cases respectively and you're now testifying in this case. Did you prepare reports in the context of the testimony -- your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you prepare a report in relation to -- well, rather, what did you -- what did your report concern in respect of your testimony in those cases?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: My report is actually an update on Dean Manning's report. It's actually called "Update to the Summary of Forensic Evidence - Exhumation of the Graves and Surface Remains Recoveries Related to Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you -- when was the first iteration of that report, in relation to what case would that have been?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I prepared my first report for Popovic et al trial, that was back I think in 2008 -- sorry, it was March 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you prepare any report in respect of the Tolimir case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I did my update of that Popovic et al trial report, and then after that, I prepared an update of Tolimir report for Karadzic report, for Karadzic trial, and now recently in June 2013 I again prepared an update of the Karadzic report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever prepare a report in relation to the Perisic case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. That was a short update on specific topic. I did prepare a report for that case but I have never testified in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated the title of your present report as it concerns the Srebrenica investigation and the summary or update to the summary on forensic evidence. In the preparation of the series of reports or I'll refer to it as a project, as it were, did you receive any kind of assistance in terms of preparing the report or drafting it or revising it, and that is any one of them, either from the beginning, back in 2009, to any iteration of it up to the one that you have prepared for this case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. As for my recent report I'm now testifying about, I did it on my own from the very beginning up until the end. Except for the charts which were created -- or actually, let's put it differently, which were prepared by military analyst but I created them manually but just they were then drafted in a special software by military analyst. Before, for other three reports I think -- or for the first two reports I prepared, I did receive an assistance from my -- our criminal intelligence -- criminal analyst, sorry, and she created the spreadsheets for DNA connections so that's what the -- that's the assistance I received over the years.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Aside from that assistance would it be fair to say that you developed, created the report independently?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, independently.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in respect of the report that you prepared for this case, can you tell the Chamber when it was come completed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It was completed on 28th of June, 2013.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Before I bring it up on e-court, I just want to ask you if you could briefly outline for the Chamber what the main purpose or purposes of this particular report is?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: The purpose of this report is to update the Trial Chamber on latest findings and facts regarding the Srebrenica-related victims, so to update the number how many of those victims have been so far identified, where they were located, in which mass graves, and how many graves. And then to update the Trial Chamber on the surface remains which were found over the years, to update Trial Chamber with number and with the places where those remains were found, and also to update Trial Chamber on the latest findings regarding the DNA connections between those graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And we will get into that in just a moment. But before we do, can you tell the Chamber what generally the sources of information were that you relied upon in order to produce your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. The main source I used was DNA, the recent DNA report on match -- their match reports, matching reports to Srebrenica-related victims and that one was provided to the OTP in April this year. So this was the main source which I was using in my report in order to find the recent and latest numbers on identified individuals from -- from the graves or surface remains found in relation to Srebrenica events. Apart from that, I've been also using documentation which was provided by the BiH authorities, namely by the BiH state prosecutor and cantonal prosecutors and also BiH Institute on Missing Persons. So these are, I think, the three main sources which I've been using in order to prepare my recent update.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just ask, Mr. Vanderpuye. Mr. Janc, by whom was the DNA report supplied to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to my understanding, as it was the case before, the DNA report was supplied to the OTP by the ICMP, International Commission on Missing Persons, which is based in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In respect of the documents you received from the BiH authorities, did you review any court files, court records, in relation to your assessment and production of the report and the data related -- the data related in it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Many of them I did review.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review any records concerning the identification of Srebrenica-related victims produced by PHR, Physicians for Human Rights?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. Also those documents, I was able to review.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are those documents referred to or referenced in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to know is, are the sources of most of the information that you considered and reviewed in preparing your report identified in the report itself either by ERN number or by title or some other means?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, they are. Most of them are referenced in my report with ERN numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the documents that are referenced in your report, were they documents that you personally reviewed or are they adopted from, perhaps, Mr. Manning's report or some other source?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Most of them I reviewed it myself and some of them were adopted from Dean Manning's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Given your experience as an investigator, both here and domestically, do you consider that the information that you used to prepare your report is reliable and accurate?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I can say it's reliable and accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You've indicated that one of the reasons that you undertook to update your previous report was to bring current the number of Srebrenica-identified individuals. First of all I want to clarify something, if I can, with you. When you say "identified," can you tell the Chamber what you mean by that, in terms of your analysis of the DNA records provided by the ICMP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. And the term "identified," I also specified in my report. It was in footnote number 3, which basically means that identified are the individuals who have been matched to -- whose DNA profiles have been matched to the missing persons so it means we have identified individuals by name and also the individuals who has unique DNA profiles which is the minority of them, which is only 142. For the purposes of this report, I included those 142 unique DNA profiles as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You indicated earlier, just a minute ago, rather, that one of the documents that you relied upon that came from the ICMP concerned the DNA match list. Did you rely on any documentation from the ICMP concerning unique DNA profiles to which no name had yet been matched?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Upon my request they provided the OTP in June this year the latest unique DNA profile list.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that the information that you relied upon in terms of assessing the number of unique individuals as shown by these discrete DNA profiles indicated in the ICMP documentation that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of the numbers that you were able to assess in preparing your report, is there any reason you can give or provide the Chamber for why there should be changes in the number of identified individuals with respect to, say, established graves over periods of time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. The identification process is ongoing by the ICMP in Bosnia, and as the time passes, new identifications are done by the ICMP, as well as new mass graves are still recovered and exhumed over so many years -- after so many years in Bosnia-Herzegovina which are related to Srebrenica events. So accordingly, the number of identified individuals is growing, is raising over the years, and that's obviously also -- also the case in my recent report where you can see that the number of identified individuals raised, if you compare it against my latest report -- my previous report, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Hopefully I'll be able to pull that up in e-court quite shortly, but in terms of any specific grave, what changes have you observed in relation to the number of individuals that you've been able to identify or -- year over year? Have they consistently gone up, have they stayed the same in some instances, have they gone down in some instances?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. Both, I would say. In respect to my report you will find one and the other. First of all I would like to clarify that some of the -- or most of the primary and secondary graves known to the ICTY have been already exhumed. Actually, those known at the beginning along Cancari Road, Hodzici Road, Liplje, those have been exhumed completely and most of those individuals have been already identified. But what happened is that, when I was reviewing the recent ICMP data, I also found instances where the number, numbers would decrease by, for example, one individual. For example, in my previous report it would be certain number of individuals and now I found there is one individual less identified in that grave. So I checked what was the reason behind and I found these reasons and we can go over them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Before I actually get to the report and show you those specific entries, in terms of the updating the grave sites, the Srebrenica-related grave sites, in this particular report, did you encounter any new information showing additional grave sites that were not the subject of your previous report? And just so that we are clear, the previous report was the one that was completed when?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, my previous report was completed in January 2012.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In relation to what case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: In relation to the Karadzic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: And, yes, in comparing those two reports, we have two new mass graves included in my recent report. One is Zalazje 2 and the other one is Kaldrmica 2010. And then we have also -- I've also included I think several for individual graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And in terms of updating the information contained in your previous report through this one completed in 2013 for this case, were you able to determine or update any artefact evidence that is referred to in your report, specifically blindfolds and ligatures?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: In my previous report I referred to the artefact and ligatures, the number of those ligatures and blindfolds found in mass graves. Reviewing my report recently, I realised that I haven't updated this number for my report, I mean this case, and so when I'm referring to the number of blindfolds and ligatures, for example, found in Cancari-related graves, this number is not correct because it's higher than what is stated in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And in terms of -- I don't want to go into the specifics of those numbers, but can you tell us roughly how the new numbers relate to what is reported in your -- what is set out in your report? Is it substantially many more blindfolds and ligatures? Slightly more? If you could give the Chamber an idea of what the difference is between the actual numbers and what is reported in your -- what is set out in your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It is more -- it's difficult to say right now if it is slightly or significantly more but I can give you the total. In graves related to -- mass graves related to Srebrenica event, there were 774 ligatures found and 593 blindfolds found.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are you able to compare that to what the totals would have been or are, rather, in your 2013 report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Not from -- from the top of my head, it would be difficult. I would need to go through my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it by the hundreds or is it by the tens of ligatures and blindfolds that have been added but not yet incorporated in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just a second. I will tell you exactly. For example, I have written for Cancari Road mass graves, for example, that around 340 ligatures and 60 blindfolds were found in these secondary graves. And now we have -- we have a total number of -- for ligatures would be 276 plus 313, and for blindfolds would be, in total, 113. So it's a kind of double number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's a significant number added. Would that be only true for the Cancari Road mass graves or would that -- a similar thing happen in relation to other graves? I don't need the details but if you say, "Yes, I remember that in that grave we found quite a substantial number of ligatures" or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would say yes, but the highest number is for sure for the Cancari Road-related graves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now I know also that you mentioned in your report the criteria that you used in order to determine whether a given grave or a given individual is associated with the Srebrenica crimes, but could you just tell us, in a nutshell, how it is you made the determination when you went through the data provided by the ICMP or FCMP or other sources, how you made a determination that either a grave or an individual was associated with the Srebrenica crimes?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. The list which is provided by the ICMP is related to -- to the victims of Srebrenica events. So they provided us a list which includes only those victims, and for the purposes of my report, then I reviewed, analysed and modified -- not modified but gave in a proper order those data. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. What about in the case of a unique DNA profile, one that -- to which a name cannot be associated? How would you or how did you attribute that unique DNA profile to the Srebrenica events, if, for example, it hadn't been matched to a name that had been reported missing in relation to those events?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. Those unique DNA profiles were provided only for the mass graves, primary and secondary, which we know are related to the fall of Srebrenica. For example, in secondary grave on Cancari Road we would find only individual which were related to the fall of Srebrenica, so it was reasonable to ask the ICMP if they can provide also the profiles of human remains or DNA profiles for which have not yet been matched to the missing persons. So that's why I was able to determine that individuals which have not been identified and they are coming from the same secondary or primary grave as the majority of the individuals or which have been already identified, that they are indeed Srebrenica-related.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The number of unique DNA profiles provided by the ICMP, has that remained consistent throughout the various iterations of your project, the various reports that you've drafted, concerning the number of identified individuals?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: The number of identified -- of unique DNA profiles drops significantly in relation to my last -- my previous report. Right now we have only 142 unique profiles. Before it was I think around 270 [Realtime transcript read in error "2700"]. The difference is that those 130 have been now identified and we have names for those 130 which were in my previous report still unique DNA profiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We have in the record here at page 16, line 17, the reference here that you said around 2700. Is that correct or did you say around 270?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, it's a mistake. I said it was 270.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. And you said 130 of those have been identified. Did those identified, those identified previously unknown DNA profiles come out of graves that were previously established to be related to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. What I'd like to do is just to go over, just very briefly before I pull up your report, what the structure of it is. So if you could just tell us how is it set out, what does it contain and what is comprised of? Just very briefly.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, it has four sections. It's a report itself of six pages long. Then I have four annexes, annex A, B, C, and confidential annex D.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Annex A, what does that contain?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It contains the actual graves, exhumations, when they were done and how many individuals were found in particular graves. So far identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. What about annex B?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Annex B contains conclusions or findings on surface remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What about annex C?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Annex C includes the DNA connections which I found.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And annex D, you said that it was confidential. What does that contain?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Correct. Annex D is a confidential part because it includes the list of individuals by names which I found on the ICMP data and because this list is confidential, provided to the OTP under restriction, that's why this annex is confidential.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to bring that up just for a moment so we can take a look at -- so the Chamber can see what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 30170. It should not be broadcast, please. There we have it. As you can see it indicates confidential annex D. If we can go to page 2 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Page 2 of the exhibit indicates graves, mass, smaller and individual graves. Does that correspond to your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in respect of these graves, are they organised -- rather, the individuals that are related to these graves, are they organised in this confidential annex?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC

utterances.text: Okay. utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we go to the next page of the document, ERN ending 0736, and that's going to be --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, first of all, we can see here a number of graves that actually continues on to page should be 5 in e-court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I've forgotten that it could be useful for the public because this is not confidential, so therefore if it could be shown, that would be preferable.

utterances.text: We have it already.

utterances.text: We do, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I was saying that this table continues on to ERN page 0738, which should be page 5 correspondingly in e-court, so what I'd like you to do is just describe for us what we have here. There is a footnote to that effect but I think it's important to have that as a matter of record.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This is the first count when I put the name the mass graves which were exhumed and those bolded ones were exhumed by the ICTY and those which are not were exhumed by the BiH authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Why was it that the case that some were exhumed by the ICTY and others exhumed by the BiH authorities, first; and second, when did the transfer, if there was one, occur?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. The authority to exhume, to further process with the exhumation activities was transferred to the BiH authorities by the ICTY sometimes in 2000, 2001. Before that, the ICTY exhumed all the primary graves and some of the secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to draw your attention to the entry for Orahovac 2, Lazete 2 in parentheses. First of all, why do we have entries here in parentheses under the names or associated with these -- with the various mass graves in some instances and in some instances not?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. For example, for Orahovac 1, Lazete 1, I'm not quite certain anymore, but as you can see, the site code, which is assigned to the mass grave before the exhumation is started, every exhumation site is assigned a site code and in this case, it was Lazete 01, and I assume because in this case, we have an exhumation site in Lazete area whereas the prisoners were kept in Orahovac school. Later on, we can see for Cancari Road we also have some names in brackets, for example, for Cancari Road 4, we have Kamenica 4. And in this case it's because the Cancari Road 4 was given a name, a site name by the ICMP -- by the ICTY, and when exhumed, it was renamed by the BiH authority to Kamenica 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I'm looking at the clock. I think we started at ten minutes past so would it be a suitable time for a break?

utterances.text: All right. utterances.text: And where we have a difference, for example, Cancari Road 4 renamed or named Kamenica 4, and we can see the site -- corresponding site code of CR04 and then in parentheticals, KAM04ZVO, who was responsible for that? utterances.text: Before we continue, could I inquire whether there is any dispute about these names referring to the same site, so Cancari Road 4 being the same as Kamenica 4.

utterances.text: So why ask who and why and -- I mean, apparently two systems did exist.

utterances.text: What I'd like to do, Mr. Janc --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is no dispute as to that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, I initially had directed your attention to Orahovac 2, Lazete 2, if we could go up the screen just for a second, and we'll see it as the -- looks like the fifth entry from the top. What I want to refer you to particularly is the number of individuals that are identified here as you've indicated in January 2012 and April 2013. You'll see here that in January 2012, 189 individuals you've indicated were identified, and a year later, in April 2013, we have 188. Can you explain that? Very briefly.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. I looked up into this issue and I found that in January 2012, I counted a unique DNA profile which was provided to us by the ICMP, and then in April 2013, or with the latest data provided by the ICMP, I didn't find that case, that individual being still the main case, on their list. So what I found is that -- but we haven't been talking about this main and reassociation as yet so I will try to explain as briefly as possible. What happened is, in the meantime, there was a new case identified -- or, actually, individual was identified in Cancari Road 6 grave and that was attributed as a main case. So what happened there is that the case which I counted before as being -- as main case in Lazete 2, as unique DNA profile, that case became reassociation to the main case in Cancari 6. So if you go down you will see you have increase in number for Cancari Road 6, so because we have now few cases, including this one, more in Cancari Road 6. Why that happened, I don't -- it's difficult to explain to me because it was change done by the ICMP. So one before it was a unique as a main case, and now it's a reassociation to a main case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And in fact we can see Cancari Road 6 reflects a change from 2012 to 2013 of 183 to 185 identified cases; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. So and I have to explain that in 2012, I haven't included that same individual into the Cancari Road 6 counting because it wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's go to the next page, please, it's ERN ending 0737, which should be page 4 in e-court. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And here what we have, I would just direct your attention to Cancari Road 12 where we can see also a decline in the number of identified individuals, and Liplje 2. Cancari Road 12 is the second line, second entry, and Liplje 2 is about a third of the way down, also in bold. Is the explanation for the decline in the number of identified individuals relative to those two graves between 2012 and 2013 attributable to similar circumstances that you've just addressed with respect to Orahovac or Lazete 2?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, first of all, I would like to correct myself explaining before the reason for Lazete 2 but that was actually what was explaining was the reason for Cancari 12, that's what happened there. For Lazete 2 we have a different problem. That was my mistake. For Lazete 2 I counted one DNA unique profile twice in my previous report, so I excluded that individual now so that's why we have a drop of one individual. Then the biggest drop we have for Liplje 2. So it's for -- for two of those cases it's more or less the same issue because the main case which two other grave site, and in one case, there was a typo mistake by the ICMP. Instead of Liplje 2 it should be Liplje 4. So we will see, for example, for Liplje 4, you have increase in number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that -- so the record just reflects it, that reflects a change from 289 identified individuals to 292; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next page, which summarises your findings. And that's ERN ending 0738. Let me see if I have my count right. That should be page 5 in e-court for the record. What I'd like to do is to take you down - yeah, we have it - to your totals. Here you have a category for graves, surface remains, others, and then identified individuals. And this is year over year from 2012 to 2013. So with respect to the number of identified individuals from Srebrenica-related graves, what is the total?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, you can see the figure here it's 6056.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And previously, as you indicated, does this include unique DNA profiles of individuals that have not been yet associated with a name?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that by virtue of the fact that those DNA profiles came from Srebrenica-related graves or from -- or based on some other reason?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, it's based on that they are coming from the Srebrenica-related graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The category for surface remains indicates a total number of individuals identified of 756. First, can you explain to the Chamber what you mean when you say "surface remains" and specifically what surface remains are included in the total that you have here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I've included in my report a special section under annex B where I am talking about the surface remains. These are human body -- body parts or the entire bodies which were found on the ground, not buried, over the years and collected by the BiH authorities, and when identified, when the identification process was done it was revealed that they were also Srebrenica victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So these are named -- or, rather, DNA profiles recovered from the surface or from shallow graves that have been DNA-matched to named individuals by the ICMP; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you identified or, rather, associated any unique DNA profiles of individuals who have not been matched to a name by the ICMP, uniques, so to speak, have you counted them among any of the surface remains that you've indicated here? Any of the 756 surface remains, do those include unique DNA profiles without names?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't because it would be very difficult to determine that these are indeed Srebrenica-related victims because in the area where the surface remains were collected, there were also instances that individuals from other events have been found and identified so -- because here we have a different story that it is with mass graves where you can say because the majority or all individuals which were identified from certain mass graves were indeed Srebrenica victims, with surface remains it's not the case, so that's why we cannot use unique DNA profiles for this specific purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, may I ask a question at this point in time? Mr. Janc, please help me with the following. On page 29, lines 19 and 20, you said, I quote, "When the identification process was done, it was revealed that they were also Srebrenica victims." Can you elaborate a little bit further? How were you able to make this -- to reach that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, these are individuals which are found on the ICRC missing list of individuals after -- of individuals related to the fall of Srebrenica and also you find them as such on the ICMP list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Have you any information that they were not combatants, were not killed during combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know, what I am providing here in my report is in relation to surface remains, these are individuals which were found on the ground. The cause of their death might be -- may vary. So some of them certainly died in combat. Some of them were executed, we have evidence on that. Some of them simply committed suicide, we have witnesses talking about that, so the cause of their death is, of course, different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Related to that topic, Mr. Janc, let me ask you about the next line in your report which concerns others. You've indicated here "others, Srebrenica-related, Kozluk surface" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Serbia-related" it's written.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Kozluk surface and Godinjske Bare. And that refers to year over year, you've come up with 37 identified individuals for 2012 and 2013. What I want to ask you about specifically is your inclusion of Kozluk surface and Godinjske Bare in this category of "others" as distinguished from surface remains which you've indicated in the line just above.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we answer that, Mr. Vanderpuye, is it indeed Serbia or is it Srebrenica? Should it be Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You are correct, it is Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that Serbia is not an incorrect thing? Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you explain to the Chamber why it is that you included Kozluk surface remains in this special category of "others" rather than the "surface remains" category that's indicated above where you found 756 individuals?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I separated them because it's -- the way they are found and the place they are found does not coincide with surface remains which I included into -- under the section -- under the annex B. When we will go over that you will understand what I'm talking about because I'm referring to specific areas where those surface remains were found. But in case of Kozluk surface, they were actually found adjacent to the mass execution site on the arena - on the Drina River embankment and actually when they were found, they were on surface but it's not really known why -- whether or not when they were placed there, these bodies, whether or not they were covered with soil and then over the time Drina River surfaced them. So that's why, because they are very close to the execution site and they may be related to that particular execution, that's why I placed them separately and I haven't counted them along with other surface remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What about the Godinjske Bare?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, the Godinjske Bare victims are related to the special incident execution which the Prosecution has the video about, so those six victims are related to that specific event. And it's -- because it's far away, actually, it's from Srebrenica, that's why I placed them in section "others," and they are also found on surface. Actually they were never buried, these bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And thank you. I was just about to ask you that. So we have here a total that you've indicated, year on year, from 2012, 6716 individuals identified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, please remain seated if you consult with counsel. A brief consultation is okay. Could you please remain seated. Please proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.text: Okay. I was just asking you about the totals that you have here, 6716 for 2012 versus 6849 for 2013. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.text: That represents all the identified individuals related to Srebrenica according to your analysis of the information provided to you by the various authorities, the ICMP, the FCMP, the Bosnian Missing Persons Institute and having reviewed exhumation records --

utterances.text: There seems to be a technical problem, as far as the audio is concerned. Mr. Mladic, can you now hear us again? Oh, is the -- one second, if you want to speak you should switch on your microphone. There seems to be something with your screen? Is that --

utterances.text: And with respect to that mixed grave, how is it that you determined that 47 individuals, the remains of 47 individuals recovered from that grave were in fact Srebrenica related rather than related to the events of 1992?

utterances.text: I'd like to go to page 2 and it should be page 2 in both the English and B/C/S.

utterances.text: The BiH Institute on Missing Persons, they are referring to what they collect on ground as cases. What does it mean in reality, you know, it might be one bone, one part of human remain, or the entire body, so we don't really know exactly what they have collected. Is it the entire body or, you know, is it just part of the body because over the years, one can imagine that body have decomposed and many body parts are only found, not the complete bodies. But what happens is then they are sent to the ICMP and after the identification is done, we'll get the actual individuals which have been identified from those body remains. So what does it mean? You know, one case can represent, I mean, in reality more than one individual or quite opposite, you know, more cases can represent only one individual. We won't really know in reality what is it, how many individuals is indeed covered with this 1033 surface remain cases which have been collected.

It's the system of how they collect the surface remains and how they record their findings is similar as to the exhumation of the mass graves, so for every single location, for every single body part or case, they will assign a site code, and if I see that in the ICMP data certain site code, I will know exactly that that site code is related to surface remains because that is information which were provided to us as such.
