utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to go to the next chart very quickly. This one I think we can make a little smaller so we can fit both on the page. That seems fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us what we are seeing here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: This is the broken down chart per execution site and now we have actually the overview of how -- how many connections is found related to particular execution site and actually primary grave and secondary grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And that's for both -- here in this case it's for both Branjevo and Pilica -- Branjevo, Pilica and Kozluk; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Between these two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question? The relatively low numbers of primary graves and secondary graves in the previous picture or here the execution site and the various graves, often if a primary grave is -- when the bodies are taken out and moved elsewhere, that means that most likely there is only a limited number of DNA material left behind in the primary grave, or at the grave site. Is that well understood? And does that explain why sometimes the numbers are relatively low of the DNA matches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, correct. That's exactly what happened there because, you know, you have a relatively small number of human remains left in the primary grave. But you -- you can see from this chart that you have in some cases really high number of cases between secondary graves because individuals were taken to secondary graves, and in two of them you can find or even one individual can be found in three different graves. So that's why you have more connections between secondary graves than --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because most of the bodily remains remained in those secondary graves, and often after some damage of being torn apart in various secondary graves, if I understand your testimony well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you're perfectly right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Two questions I want to ask you in relation to this particular chart. The first is, at the very bottom of the screen we can see a DNA connection between two secondary graves to both Branjevo military farm, Pilica and Kozluk --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- which the Chamber has received evidence are independent primary mass grave sites.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So I'd like to ask you if you were able to provide an explanation as to how it is that you would have a DNA connection between secondary graves related to independent, separate primary mass grave sites. The second part is for an explanation as to why Liplje 2, although is a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps -- or are the questions so related that we cannot understand the answer to the first question. Let's take them one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first question is about the horizontal link between the Kozluk and Branjevo cases.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We have to understand that those two primary graves have been re-exhumed at about the same time, and according to my understanding from the investigation itself, the same transport means have been used during reburial operation. So in this case, it might be easily that this is contamination, that some body parts from one particular primary grave have remained on the truck while there has been exhumation, exhumation of the other primary graves. That's one of the possible conclusions why these appeared as such. And the same would be the case for when you started this question for Liplje 2, connection between Liplje 2 and Cancari 3, it might be the same kind of explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. It obviates the need for my second question. If we could just go to the next chart, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the third one, the last one, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, there are actually five. Perhaps I can go to the last one and that might be more efficient because this incorporates some of the previous findings, although it is, as you can see, a somewhat --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do it as you wish but I expect you now to put focused questions to the witness and what we can see and read is there, what needs an explanation as with the last few questions certainly assists. And could you please finish within the next five to seven minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Janc, we are now at chart 4C. And this concerns Glogova 2 and Glogova 1. First of all, what am I looking at here? What do we see?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: As with previous charts this is just a -- as you can see a network of connections between primary grave Glogova and related secondary graves. So that's how many connections have been established between those primary and secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So there were no connections that you were able to establish between Glogova 1 and either Bljeceva 1 or Bljeceva 2?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. There is only connections established between Glogova 2 and Bljeceva 1 and Bljeceva 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And the blue lines that we see between them represent exactly what?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: These are connections between the secondary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are these subsumed in the previous charts, particularly chart 4B, and 4A, which preceded this one?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Chart 4A would represent only the connections between primary and secondary graves, and the chart 4B would represent only the connections between those secondary graves and this is the overall chart of both together.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of the -- in terms of the designation of a primary --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise for the interruption. But I'm advised that my client would like to use the facilities, the restroom, and was asking to be excused for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, he is excused. Does he want us to wait or could we continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can continue. Then, Mr. Mladic is excused for a moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of the designation of primary and secondary graves that we see here depicted in this section, should we take it that that designation derives from other information that is not shown in this particular section of which you were made privy or had a chance to review?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And does the evidence as presented in your report with respect to the DNA connection that you were able to establish corroborate or is it consistent with the other forensic evidence that you reviewed concerning what graves relate to which?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, it is perfectly consistent with previous findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you find any inconsistencies in the data that you reviewed versus the other forensic data such as artefacts, anthropological issues, that you reviewed concerning the exhumations of these graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you describe these graves or the relationship of primary and secondary graves in a map that you prepared in relation to your previous testimony?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I can just show you, and this will be my last exhibit, Mr. President, 65 ter -- before I do that let me just tender -- yes, let me tender the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection to the report but there is no B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It will be MFIed, I understand, but the translation is still pending, Mr. President, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, the number assigned?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 30169 will be MFIed P1987, pending B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And keeps that status until we have received in e-court the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could show the witness, please, 65 ter 19929.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is this the map -- is this the map that you prepared in order to depict the relationship of primary and -- primary mass graves, secondary mass graves and so on, based on the information that you reviewed in connection with your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just zoom in at the top of the map, we can see a number of arrows and directions and groups of certain graves. Are all of these graves represented in your current report, your -- the one that you completed in June?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can go down the page, we can see yet another series of arrows and graves. Are all of these graves contained in your current report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: These and a few more.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And so there are graves that are referred to in your report that are not contained in this map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, because this is an earlier map which would correspond with my earlier reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does this map depict in general terms the movement or direction of bodies, remains, from the main mass grave sites, the disturbed mass grave sites referred to in annex A, to the secondary grave sites?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, correct, correct. This is what the red arrows are showing us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's accurate to date?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to tender this document, 65 ter 19929.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that will conclude my direct examination with your leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The number to be assigned, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1988, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1988 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, Ms. Stewart informs me that I should inform the Court that 65 ter 6358A, P1985, has now been uploaded to e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore where it was assigned the MFI status, it is now admitted into evidence under the number, Mr. Registrar, you had provisionally assigned was?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P1986, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1986 therefore is now admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, P1985 is the correct number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1985, that's one page of 65 ter 06358.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then P1985 is admitted into evidence. P1986 was already admitted into evidence. Then I wonder whether it would not be wiser to take the break now and that you start your cross-examination after the break, Mr. Ivetic. I had forgotten that we lost half an hour in the beginning, a little bit over half an hour. If we could continue for the next 25 minutes, Mr. Ivetic, or would you like to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We can continue, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Janc, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic and you'll find him to your left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, apart from testifying before the Tribunal as a witness for the Prosecution in several cases relating to Srebrenica, have you had occasion to testify as a witness, whether fact or expert, in any other proceedings?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: You mean before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Before or after.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I testified before the national court in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In terms of that prior testimony before the national court in Slovenia, did you use any of the similar methodology or reporting styles as in the reports that you have testified for in front of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It's difficult to say that I've used the similar or same methodology because the cases were different, of different types, what I've been investigating then and what's been investigating here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In relation to your time spent at the Office of the Prosecutor of the Tribunal, did your duties include interviewing witnesses and potential suspects for ongoing cases?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were any of these interviews related to the case against General Ratko Mladic, that is to say, related to the indictment against General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I would say yes because they were related to the entire Srebrenica investigation and they would be related to your client as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. While you were employed with the Office of the Prosecutor, were you ever tasked with assisting in the drafting or amending of any indictments?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were any of the investigations that you took part in while at the Office of the Prosecutor related to verifying any claims of ethnic Muslim victims who had been killed by fellow ethnic Muslim forces in Srebrenica, either in the enclave itself or during the march of the Bosnian Muslim column of men to Tuzla after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you about a different topic. Are you familiar from your work of a military and civil protection concept in the former SFRY called sanitisation of the terrain in English or "asanacija terena" in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yeah, I heard about that concept, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this concept would involve the obligation to clear from a former combat zone or battlefield all artefacts of a battle including weapons, munitions, debris, and biological remains, whether human or of animals, and in the case of human remains, bury the same?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I'm sure it includes some of those but I cannot really affirm it includes everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. We have had some testimony of another witness in these proceedings, RM306, who testified that pursuant to the legal obligations of the SFRY Law on Civil Protection - and this can be found at transcript page 11464 through 11465 - the bodies and remains recovered by asanacija would be buried in communal or mass graves rather than individual graves. Does this accord with your knowledge of asanacija in the SFRY system?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I can't really say it -- it's -- I don't really have knowledge about specific term, what would include.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, I want to ask you just briefly about the time period of June 2003 through June 2004, while you were in the European Police Mission to Bosnia as an advisor to the criminal investigations department of the Republika Srpska MUP in Banja Luka. Did any of your work as an advisor at that time involve any investigations by the RS MUP in Banja Luka relating to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I want to take some time to inquire about the work that you did in preparing your report. In relation to the material that you read, you identified witness statements and other -- I think you referred to some sort of internal reports that were prepared. First of all, could you identify for us, when you referred to internal writings or memoranda, what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, this was a question when I was asked what kind of documents I have been in general reviewing while working for the OTP and one of those records would be also these internal records, so you would find, for example, spreadsheets on conducting investigations, various note to files or this kind of internal correspondence or internal investigative documentation I was referring to. But in terms of my report, for drafting my report, whatever I have used, I have referenced it in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in relation to the witness statements that you would have reviewed to come to conclusions, did you -- let's put it this way, the witness statement that you read, did they comprise a percentage of the available statements relating to the events in Srebrenica or were they all of the available statements relating to Srebrenica? Is there any way you could identify for us what portion of the totality of the statements you would have reviewed or had access to for purposes of doing your work?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I did have access to all of those statements, or at least to those who -- which were not restricted. And even if they were restricted, if they were related to Srebrenica events I would get access to those. So the total number, I don't know how many of them I have reviewed but it might be quite many in the period of five years.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to those that you did review, were these selected by someone else for you or were they all ones that you selected to review for whatever reason you selected them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It was mainly selected by me. You know there were definitely instances where someone would ask to you review a certain statement for certain things, but if I'm focused on my report now it was, you know, basically selected by me, especially when I was trying to establish or verify certain facts, yes, that's what I've been doing. So I've been trying to locate them myself and to review them myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you've also identified here today, and I believe each of your reports makes clear that they are a continuation of the work of Mr. Dean Manning. Did you have any communications with Mr. Manning for purposes of performing your work and preparing these reports as a continuation of the work that he did?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I had had a contact with him, I'd say personal contacts perhaps, I think, two times in my life so far. So first time when he came here in 2007 to prepare his update for Popovic trial, at that time, we did discuss the issues but for -- just because I was curious of what he had been doing and what he had achieved and everything. That had nothing to do with my report which I drafted later, and at that time I was talking to him I didn't even know that I would be tasked to do that. So for the second time, I think I saw him after he finished his testimony in one of the cases and we just briefly chatted but not about the report, so I haven't received any kind of directions or anything from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, did you just take the work of Mr. Manning as a finished product and work from there or did you go back and actually try to double check or verify any of the work of Mr. Manning arising from his reports?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: There were certain verifications needed, but not -- not many, I would say, because it's -- my report is focusing, you know, on numbers, itself, and connections and surface remains, and this is the area, let's say, surface remains, which I modified in terms of what he concluded in his earlier reports so because he didn't have enough information available in respect to that portion of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to now move on to another one of the sources that you cited, the ICMP reports. In relation to those -- excuse me, I should say lists. In relation to the ICMP lists, did you undertake to perform any investigation of the identifications that were made by ICMP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes. In some cases, yes, you know. In majority of cases, no, but in some cases yes, I did do a kind of investigation, when there was a kind of a situation which would not be consistent with findings in -- in our investigation. And I detected some cases in their list, in their earlier lists, where they would identify individuals as being related to Srebrenica and they were actually -- and actually they were not. Actually they were victims of some other incidents from 1993, 1992, and in their subsequent updates which they provided to us, they actually removed those individuals from the list. Some of them were identified by themselves but, yes, there were such instances but, you know, there were a small number of such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In relation to those instances where you did check and you did find errors of how ICMP identified these individuals and how your own investigations identified these individuals, did you contact ICMP? Did you have a role in the subsequent lists that changed that information?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: I'm quite sure, you know, I'm not certain but I'm quite sure that this information was forwarded to the ICMP and they rechecked their list and they reverified these facts. But nevertheless, if I identified such individuals, I haven't included them into my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you also identified various BiH authorities as being a source for your reports and I want to just clarify the -- you did not in direct examination include the BiH Ministry of Defence. Can we conclude from that that you did not consult with the Ministry of Defence of the BiH for purpose of generating your reports?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Not me personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the decision not to consult the BiH Ministry of Defence, was that a decision that you reached by yourself or was it a decision reached by someone else at the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: No. There was no -- it's not about decision here. It's about the need. Because I did know that at that time there were inquiries made at the Ministry of Defence by our demographics unit and I did get information from their side about what they have been provided with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. In the course of your work in preparing your reports, did you have occasion to review any of the Defence demographic expert submissions from either the Popovic or any of the other cases that you were involved in at the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, I think I did review them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As part of your investigative work and in preparing your reports, did you have occasion to take into account casualties that may have occurred as part of the Bosnian Muslim column of men that left Srebrenica in July 1995 and attempted to break through the Serb lines to get to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what kinds of sources did you consult to gain information about the casualties that occurred to members of the Bosnian Muslim column of men that attempted to break through to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes, various sources. You know, there we have several statements about those casualties, what happened to certain individuals breaking through. Then for the purposes of my report, one of the main sources was, of course, the data on surface remains because many of them were just left behind, and this is one of the main sources. Also, there were sources, some witnesses, some expert witnesses, testified in this courtroom saying about the rough numbers of those casualties. So I did take into consideration those sources, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'd like to now review something from one of the prior cases that you testified on with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could have 1D1196 in e-court. That should be the 4 May Popovic transcript, and if we can have the page 27 in e-court, which should correlate to transcript page 33593 of that case's transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will endeavour to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to ask you, from line 9 onward, to follow along with me as I go over this prior testimony of yours. "Sir, I'm going to ask you a couple of preliminary questions. First, I'd like to know, is it fair to state that the number of missing persons includes the people who have perished as a result of land mines, suicide, or the result of legitimate combat engagements in your analysis? "A. Yes, most probably, yes. "Q. Do you know what number that is? "A. No, I don't know the exact number, but I would say most of the cases are related to the surface remains. "Q. Okay. With the -- including the surface remains, do you know of any evidence - because I know you've read as your addendum, I think, reflected various witness statements and other documents and testimonies in this case - do you know that the number resulting from combat engagements, suicides, and land mines is roughly anywhere from 1.000 to 2.000? "A. No, I can't say. "Q. Would be reasonable in your view? "A. Closer to 1.000, perhaps not to 2.000." And now, sir, first I have to ask you if you can confirm that this transcript selection appears to accurately depict your answers to these questions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And are the answers as reflected given truthful so that you would so testify again today if asked the same questions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could turn to the next page of this transcript, so it's page 28 in e-court, correlating to transcript page 33594, I would like to revisit the questions and answers there beginning at line 1 with you. "Q. Here is what Mr. Butler said -- you know who he is; right? "A. Yes, I know. "Q. He testified on the 23rd of January, 2008, and it starts on page 20212. And we had a little discussion about that with him, but particularly on page 20251, on lines 12 through 14, for my learned friends, in discussing legitimate combat engagements with respect to the Bosnian Muslim military column that was going through Susnjari and trying to make it through Kladanj and Tuzla, he says, quote, in answer to my question: 'Yes, sir. I mean, I think the 1.000 to 2.000 number would be reasonable with respect to the combat casualties, starting, you know, from 12 July through the life span of the column which is effectively 18 July.' "A. Yes. "Q. Do you agree or disagree with Mr. Butler's military analytical assessment that the casualties as a result of the military column was anywhere from 1.000 to 2.000? "A. Based on the information we have now, I still think it's closer to 1.000. "Q. Okay. And that's based on what, sir? "A. Based on the identifications we have for surface remains, which is 648 now." First of all, sir, does this excerpt appear to accurately depict the answers that you gave to these questions in the Popovic case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if those answers were truthful so that you would so testify again today?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, just to clarify, the Mr. Butler that was discussed in this transcript, is this the person, a military expert, whom you had referenced today without giving his name as being one of the sources for the investigation that you undertook?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you seem to rely here on the number of identified surface remains for your lower estimate of closer to 1.000 killed in the column. Would you agree with me, looking at the surface remains, that -- that there are about 300 that have not been identified by DNA?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: 300 of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Surface remains, recovered surface remains. Or surface remain cases, I should say.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: It's difficult to say how many because we don't know how many -- actually we do know. I did a statistic on that and I will tell you. For 756 individuals, it was -- I think it was 1.1 case needed for one individual to be identified. So, for example, if you have 1100 individual cases, that would mean - this is again statistically speaking - around 1.000 individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So the question that I have for you, then, is your definition of casualties from the column is almost exclusively, then, those that are qualified as surface remains; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC
utterances.text: Not necessarily but mostly yes. Because what we have in other graves, there are evidence that these are people who has suffered from the executions. And then we have the section where we have 756 people found on the surface, and of course there is still I think around 800 individuals who are still missing, not being found or exhumed, and identified, so we don't know what happened with those 800. So it may be that they are one day found on the surface and they will be included into that counting but it may also be that they will be found in mass graves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I'm looking at the clock. I think it's time for us to adjourn. But before doing so, Mr. Janc, we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at half past 9.00 -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, at page 83, line 8, you are recorded as having said: "So, for example, if you have 1100 individual cases, that would mean - this is again statistically speaking - around 1.000 individuals."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say 1100?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it's 1.000. For example, if you have 1.000 identified individuals and for one individual, statistically speaking, by now it's 1.1 case needed so it will -- it means that 1.000 individuals will occupy 1.100 cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I understand you well that means that if you have 1100 cases, that there would be a hundred of those cases which could be linked to a hundred of the remaining cases which would reduce the total number of persons to 1.000, there being 100 double countings due to two cases referring to one person? Perhaps I have not been very clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you know, it's again statistically it's difficult to say how many of them have not yet been tested but still, yes, statistically speaking, you need 1100 cases for 1.000 individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then having verified this, we would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. I would like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given today or testimony still to be given tomorrow. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile before we adjourn, and seeking the indulgence of all those assisting us, I'd like to very briefly deal with a few matters. I really keep it short. The Defence has requested an extension of 60 days to respond to the Prosecution's motion to admit evidence from the bar table concerning the SRK and VRS materials related to the siege of Sarajevo. The Chamber notes in this regard that while the motion concerns a large number of documents, most are only one or two pages in length. The Chamber therefore grants the request in part, allowing an additional 30 days to respond and hereby sets a new deadline of the 13th of September. The Defence has also requested an extension of 21 days to respond to the Prosecution's 32nd motion to admit evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis, and as a preliminary matter, the Chamber notes that although the Defence motion makes a single reference to a requested deadline of the 4th of October, the Chamber considers this to be a typo, since the remainder of the motion refers to a 21-day extension which would make the new deadline the 4th of September. After considering the relative length and the complexity of the Prosecution's motion, the Chamber hereby grants the Defence request for a 21-day extension and sets a new deadline of the 4th of September. The last issue I will deal with. On the 15th of August the Defence filed a motion for an extension of the deadline to respond to the Prosecution's 11th motion to add documents to the 65 ter exhibit list. The Chamber notes that the Defence motion appears to mistakenly request both an extension of 30 days, with a deadline of the 16th of September, and an extension of 60 days with a deadline of the 14th of October. The Chamber is seeking clarification from the Defence on this matter before we will be able to decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we let you know first thing in the morning, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First thing in the morning and then you'll have to wait for a decision until we have received that information. Then we will adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, the 20th of August, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III.
